title: Check yourself: The calls that wait and the calls that do not

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A pipeline step runs `claude "Analyze this pull request"` and hangs. What fixes it?

options.text: Point its input at an empty file so it cannot wait
options.says: Ruled out because it is a workaround: "Redirecting standard input from an empty file is a Unix workaround that does not change how Claude Code runs."

options.text: Export an environment variable that selects headless mode
options.says: Ruled out because no such variable exists: "There is no headless environment variable and no `--batch` flag on the command line".

options.text: Add a batch flag so the call is queued
options.says: Ruled out for the same reason: "There is no headless environment variable and no `--batch` flag on the command line".

options.text: Add the print flag so that the run answers and exits
options.says: `-p` is the documented way to run without a person.

questions.stem: A pipeline has a gate that stops merges until it passes and a dependency digest that people read on Monday. Which calls move to batch?

options.text: Just the one nobody waits on, while the other stays in real time
options.says: Nobody waits for the digest and a developer waits for the gate.

options.text: Both of them, with polling to find out when the gate is ready
options.says: Ruled out because waiting is the problem: "Polling a batch does not make it finish sooner."

options.text: Neither of them, since the results of a batch arrive in any order
options.says: Ruled out because matching exists: "Results of a batch come back matched by `custom_id`, so their order is no reason to avoid it."

options.text: Both of them, with a fallback to real time when a batch is slow
options.says: Ruled out because it adds a path: "A fallback to real time when a batch is slow adds a second path and a second bill".

questions.stem: To which jobs does the audit's `no-print-flag` finding apply?

options.text: Any job whose api is batch, whatever its command
options.says: Ruled out for the same reason: "the `-p` rule applies to commands that start with `claude` and not to a script".

options.text: A command that starts `python` and submits a script without `-p`
options.says: Ruled out because a script is not covered: "the `-p` rule applies to commands that start with `claude` and not to a script".

options.text: A command that starts `claude` and has neither `-p` nor `--print`
options.says: The finding is about the command line: "`no-print-flag`: a command that starts `claude` without `-p` or `--print`."

options.text: Any job that a developer waits for, whatever its command
options.says: Ruled out because waiting has its own finding: "`blocking-batch`: a job someone waits for that runs as a batch."
